fit: soybean oil comparator and essential voice tremor
assessment: The original identifies the matched placebo as soybean oil and excludes Parkinson disease. Both placebo acoustic means fell slightly, while octanoic acid produced larger changes. Blinded perceptual comparisons were inconclusive and the design has no oil-free arm.

fit: formulated curcumin and 400-m walking outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The reported improvement was +0.014 versus +0.103 m/s. Exploratory unadjusted 95% CI −0.188 to +0.010 m/s for the between-arm change difference. Grip and the journal's broader motor battery and knee torque estimates lean the other way. Registry and article are the same pilot.

fit: high-oleic sunflower oil active comparator and cognitive outcomes
assessment: DHA shortened working-memory response time by 0.36 SD relative to oil. Working-memory score and attention intervals span zero. The oil arm did not slow overall, and the trial gives no independent sunflower effect, pressing grade or Parkinson estimate.

fit: formulated curcumin and 0–10 pain outside Parkinson disease
assessment: The registry reports pain means 0.97 to 0.20 with curcumin and 1.30 to 1.60 with placebo, difference in change −1.07/10 from rounded means. No change variance or between-arm analysis, and neither culinary turmeric nor Parkinson-specific pain was measured.
